title: Canada-resident NRI trapped using a fake ID, demand of 50 thousand dollars, Ghaziabad police's big action against a sextortion gang

reading.body:
This is a case of alleged sextortion in which a synthetic video was used as a threat rather than as a lure. The reported sequence is a fake social media profile, a recorded video call, a demand for money, and a threat to circulate AI-generated explicit video if payment was refused. The generative tool appears at the coercion stage, after contact had already been made, and its role was to make the threat credible enough to be paid.

The failure here is not a model asserting something false. It is a person using a generative system to manufacture compromising material about a real individual and presenting it as real. Nothing in the reporting describes a platform or model failing on its own, and no automated check is described at any point in the chain. Catching this kind of use would require detection at the point of creation or distribution, and the reports do not establish that any such detection occurred.

What is not established is guilt. The arrests, the FIR, and the police account of the gang's history are allegations, and no court finding is reported. The claim that the gang was active since 2023 and cheated hundreds of people rests on police statements, and the link between the accused and the 130 bank accounts is likewise an investigative assertion rather than a proven fact.

summary:
A Jamia Millia Islamia student named Md Faisal, 22, and three associates from Muzaffarnagar were arrested in Ghaziabad for allegedly extorting a Canada-based NRI. Police said the gang created a fake Facebook profile, recorded the victim in a compromising position during a Sept 10 video call, then demanded $50,000 and threatened to circulate AI-generated explicit videos. The victim contacted the cybercrime team on Sept 17, and the accused's mobile number was linked to 40 fraud complaints.

Police registered an FIR under the BNS and IT Act and arrested four gang members on Friday, while some accomplices remain absconding. Investigators said the gang had been active since 2023, cheated hundreds of people, and used mule accounts and AI videos. Their phones revealed links to at least 130 bank accounts holding Rs 6.6 crore.
